hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 946

chapter.arabicTitle: باب الموعظة عند القبر
chapter.englishTitle: Admonition beside the Grave

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu `Amr (also called Abu `Abdullah and also Abu Laila) from `Uthman bin `Affan (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 After the burial of a dead man, the Prophet ﷺ would stand by the grave and say, "Ask Allah to forgive your brother and supplicate for him for steadfastness because he is being questioned (about his deeds) now."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abu `Amr (also called Abu `Abdullah and also Abu Laila) from `Uthman bin `Affan (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
After the burial of a dead man, the Prophet ﷺ would stand by the grave and say, "Ask Allah to forgive your brother and supplicate for him for steadfastness because he is being questioned (about his deeds) now."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: عن أبي عمرو -وقيل: أبو عبد الله، وقيل: أبو ليلى- عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه قال: كان النبي ﷺى الله عليه وسلم الله عليه وسلم الله عليه وسلم  إذا فرغ من دفن الميت وقف عليه، وقال: "استغفروا لأخيكم وسلوا له التثبيت، فإنه الآن يسأل" ((رواه أبو داود)).
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 946

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 947

chapter.arabicTitle: باب الدعاء للميت بعد دفنه والقعود عند قبره ساعة للدعاء له والاستغفار والقراءة
chapter.englishTitle: Supplication for the Deceased after his Burial

hadiths.englishRaw:
'Amr bin Al-'as (May Allah be pleased with him) used to say:
 "When you have buried me, keep standing near my grave till (for the time it takes to) a camel is slaughtered and its meat is distributed, so that I may feel your nearness and know what to reply to the angels sent by my Rubb."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: 'Amr bin Al-'as (May Allah be pleased with him) used to say:
hadiths.body:
"When you have buried me, keep standing near my grave till (for the time it takes to) a camel is slaughtered and its meat is distributed, so that I may feel your nearness and know what to reply to the angels sent by my Rubb."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنه قال: إذا دفنتمونى، فأقيموا حول قبري قدر ما تنحر  جذور، ويقسم لحمها حت أستأنس بكم، وأعلم ماذا أراجع به رسل ربي" ((رواه مسلم. وقد سبق بطوله)). وقال الشافعي رحمه الله: ويستحب أن يقرأ عنده شيء من القرآن، وإن ختموا القرآن عنده كان حسناً. وقال الشافعي رحمه الله: ويستحب أن يقرأ عنده شيء من القرآن، وإن ختموا القرآن عنده كان حسناً.
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 947

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 948

chapter.arabicTitle: باب الدعاء للميت بعد دفنه والقعود عند قبره ساعة للدعاء له والاستغفار والقراءة
chapter.englishTitle: Supplication for the Deceased after his Burial

hadiths.englishRaw:
'Aishah (May Allah be pleased with her) reported:
 A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "My mother has died suddenly. I think that if she were able to talk (alive) she would have given in Sadaqah (charity). So, if I give Sadaqah now on her behalf, will she get the reward?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Yes (she will be rewarded for that)."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: 'Aishah (May Allah be pleased with her) reported:
hadiths.body:
A man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "My mother has died suddenly. I think that if she were able to talk (alive) she would have given in Sadaqah (charity). So, if I give Sadaqah now on her behalf, will she get the reward?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Yes (she will be rewarded for that)."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن رجلاً قال للنبي ﷺ : إن أمي افتلتت نفسها وأراها لو تكلمت، تصدقت، فهل لها أجر إن تصدقت عنها؟ قال: "نعم" ((متفق عليه))
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 948

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 949

chapter.arabicTitle: باب الصدقة عن الميت والدعاء له
chapter.englishTitle: Charity on behalf of the Deceased and Praying for him

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "When a man dies, his deeds come to an end, except for three: A continuous charity, knowledge by which people derive benefit, pious son who prays for him."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "When a man dies, his deeds come to an end, except for three: A continuous charity, knowledge by which people derive benefit, pious son who prays for him."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ  قال: “إذا مات الأنسان انقطع عمله إلا من ثلاث: صدقة جارية، أو علم ينتفع به، أو ولد صالح يدعو له" ((رواه مسلم)).
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 949

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 950

chapter.arabicTitle: باب الصدقة عن الميت والدعاء له
chapter.englishTitle: Charity on behalf of the Deceased and Praying for him

hadiths.englishRaw:
Anas (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 Some Companions happened to pass by a funeral procession (bier) and they praised him (the deceased). The Prophet ﷺ said, "He will certainly enter it." Then they passed by another funeral procession and they spoke ill of the deceased. The Prophet ﷺ said, "He will certainly enter it." `Umar bin Al-Khattab (May Allah be pleased with him) said: "(O Messenger of Allah,) what do you mean by `He will certainly enter it?'' He ﷺ replied, "You praised the first person, so he will enter Jannah; and you spoke ill of the second person, so he will enter Hell. You are Allah's witnesses on earth."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Anas (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
Some Companions happened to pass by a funeral procession (bier) and they praised him (the deceased). The Prophet ﷺ said, "He will certainly enter it." Then they passed by another funeral procession and they spoke ill of the deceased. The Prophet ﷺ said, "He will certainly enter it." `Umar bin Al-Khattab (May Allah be pleased with him) said: "(O Messenger of Allah,) what do you mean by `He will certainly enter it?'' He ﷺ replied, "You praised the first person, so he will enter Jannah; and you spoke ill of the second person, so he will enter Hell. You are Allah's witnesses on earth."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: مروا بجنازة، فأثنوا عليها خيراً، فقال النبي ﷺ الله عليه وسلمى الله عليه وسلم  الله عليه وسلم : "وجبت”، ثم مروا بأخرى، فأثنوا عليها شراً، فقال النبي ﷺى الله عليه وسلم الله عليه وسلم الله عليه وسلم : "وجبت" فقال عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: ما وجبت؟ قال: "هذا أثنيتم عليه خيراً، فوجبت له الجنة، وهذا أثنيتم عليه شراً فوجبت عليه النار، أنتم شهداء الله في الأرض” ((متفق عليه)).
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 950

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 951

chapter.arabicTitle: باب ثناء الناس علي الميت
chapter.englishTitle: Praising the Deceased

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abul-Aswad (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 I came to Al- Madinah, and while I was sitting beside 'Umar bin Al-Khattab, a funeral procession passed by. The people praised the deceased, and 'Umar bin Al-Khattab said: "He will certainly enter it." Then another funeral procession passed by and the people praised the deceased. 'Umar bin Al-Khattab (May Allah be pleased with him) said: "He will certainly enter it." A third funeral procession passed by and the people spoke ill of the deceased. He said: "He will certainly enter it." I (Abul-Aswad) asked: "O Amir Al-Mu'minin (i.e., Leader of the Believers)! What do you mean by 'He will certainly enter it'?" He replied: "I said the same as was said by the Prophet ﷺ. He ﷺ said, 'If four persons testify the righteousness of a Muslim, Allah will grant him Jannah.' We asked: 'If three persons testify his righteousness?' He ﷺ replied, 'Even three'. Then we asked: 'If two?' He ﷺ replied, 'Even two.' We did not ask him (regarding the testimony) of one."

[Al-Bukhari]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abul-Aswad (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
I came to Al- Madinah, and while I was sitting beside 'Umar bin Al-Khattab, a funeral procession passed by. The people praised the deceased, and 'Umar bin Al-Khattab said: "He will certainly enter it." Then another funeral procession passed by and the people praised the deceased. 'Umar bin Al-Khattab (May Allah be pleased with him) said: "He will certainly enter it." A third funeral procession passed by and the people spoke ill of the deceased. He said: "He will certainly enter it." I (Abul-Aswad) asked: "O Amir Al-Mu'minin (i.e., Leader of the Believers)! What do you mean by 'He will certainly enter it'?" He replied: "I said the same as was said by the Prophet ﷺ. He ﷺ said, 'If four persons testify the righteousness of a Muslim, Allah will grant him Jannah.' We asked: 'If three persons testify his righteousness?' He ﷺ replied, 'Even three'. Then we asked: 'If two?' He ﷺ replied, 'Even two.' We did not ask him (regarding the testimony) of one."

[Al-Bukhari]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن أبي الأسود قال: قدمت المدينة، فجلست إلي عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه فمرت بهم جنازة، فأثني علي صاحبها خيراً فقال عمر: وجبت، ثم مر بأخرى، فأثني علي صاحبها خيراً، فقال عمر: وجبت، ثم مر بالثالثة، فأثني علي صاحبها شراً، فقال عمر: وجبت: قال أبو الأسود: فقلت: وما وجبت يا أمير المؤمنين؟ قال: قلت كما قال النبي ﷺى الله عليه وسلم  الله عليه وسلم : “أيما مسلم شهد له أربعة بخير، أدخله الله الجنة: فقلنا: وثلاثة؟ قال: “وثلاثة" فقلنا: واثنان؟ قال: "واثنان" ثم لم نسأله عن الواحد" ((رواه البخاري)).
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 951

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 952

chapter.arabicTitle: باب ثناء الناس علي الميت
chapter.englishTitle: Praising the Deceased

hadiths.englishRaw:
Anas (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Any Muslim who loses three children before they reach the age of maturity, will be granted Jannah by Allah, the Exalted, out of His Mercy for them."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Anas (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Any Muslim who loses three children before they reach the age of maturity, will be granted Jannah by Allah, the Exalted, out of His Mercy for them."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: عن أنس رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ : "ما من مسلم يموت له ثلاثة لم يبلغوا الحنث إلا ادخله الله الجنة بفضل رحمته إياهم" ((متفق عليه)).
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 952

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 953

chapter.arabicTitle: باب فضل من مات له أولاد صغار
chapter.englishTitle: Superiority of one who is Bereaved of his Infants

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "A Muslim whose three children die (in infancy) will not be touched by the Fire (of Hell) except for the fulfillment of Allah's Oath."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.

[Allah's Oath here refers to His Ayah: "There is not one of you but will cross over it (Hell)." (19:71) And the crossing will be across the 'Bridge' set over the Hell.]
hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "A Muslim whose three children die (in infancy) will not be touched by the Fire (of Hell) except for the fulfillment of Allah's Oath."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.

[Allah's Oath here refers to His Ayah: "There is not one of you but will cross over it (Hell)." (19:71) And the crossing will be across the 'Bridge' set over the Hell.]
boldSegments: [Allah's Oath here refers to His Ayah: "There is not one of you but will cross over it (Hell)." (19:71) And the crossing will be across the 'Bridge' set over the Hell.]
hadiths.arabic: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ : “لا يموت لأحد من المسلمين ثلاثة من الولد لا تمسه النار إلا تحلة القسم" ((متفق عليه))
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 953

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 954

chapter.arabicTitle: باب فضل من مات له أولاد صغار
chapter.englishTitle: Superiority of one who is Bereaved of his Infants

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah! Only men benefit from your talks, so please fix a day for us, to teach us the knowledge which Allah has taught you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fixed a day and directed them to assemble. When they gathered, the Prophet ﷺ went to them and taught them what Allah had taught him. He ﷺ then said, "Any woman of you whose three children die (in infancy) they will be a guard for her against Fire (of Hell)." One of the women asked: "What if she loses two?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied, "Even two."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah! Only men benefit from your talks, so please fix a day for us, to teach us the knowledge which Allah has taught you." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ fixed a day and directed them to assemble. When they gathered, the Prophet ﷺ went to them and taught them what Allah had taught him. He ﷺ then said, "Any woman of you whose three children die (in infancy) they will be a guard for her against Fire (of Hell)." One of the women asked: "What if she loses two?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ replied, "Even two."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري رضي الله عنه قال: جاءت امرأة إلي رسول الله ﷺ ، فقالت: يا رسول الله ذهب الرجال بحديثك، فاجعل لنا مننفسك يوماً ناتيك فيه تعلمنا مما علمك الله، قال: “اجتمعن يوم كذا وكذا” فاجتمعن، فأتاهن النبي ﷺ   فعلمهن مما علمه الله، ثم قال: "ما منكن من امرأة تقدم ثلاثة من الولد إلا كانوا لها حجاباً من النار" فقالت امرأة: واثنين؟ فقال رسول الله ﷺ  “واثنين” ((متفق عليه)).
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 954

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 955

chapter.arabicTitle: باب فضل من مات له أولاد صغار
chapter.englishTitle: Superiority of one who is Bereaved of his Infants

hadiths.englishRaw:
Ibn `Umar (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
 When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions reached Al-Hijr, the dwellings of the Thamud people, he admonished his Companions (saying), "Do not pass by these people who are being tormented, without weeping, lest the punishment should befall you as it had befallen them."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Ibn `Umar (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
hadiths.body:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions reached Al-Hijr, the dwellings of the Thamud people, he admonished his Companions (saying), "Do not pass by these people who are being tormented, without weeping, lest the punishment should befall you as it had befallen them."

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله ﷺ  قال لأصحابه -يعني لما وصلوا الحجر: ديار ثمود-: "لا تدخلوا علي هؤلاء المعذبين إلا أن تكونوا باكين، فإن لم تكونوا باكين، فلا تدخلوا عليهم، لا يصيبكم ما أصابهم” ((متفق عليه)) وفي رواية قال: لما مر رسول الله ﷺ  بالحجر قال: "لا تدخلوا مساكن الذين ظلموا أنفسهم أن يصيبكم ما أصابهم إلا ان تكونوا باكين" ثم قنع رسول الله ﷺ  رأسه وأسرع  السير حتي أجاز الوادي.
references: Book of Visiting the Sick, Hadith 955

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 956

chapter.arabicTitle: باب استحباب الخروج يوم الخميس واستحبابه أول النهار
chapter.englishTitle: The Desirability of setting on a Journey on Thursday in the Early part of the Day

hadiths.englishRaw:
Ka'b bin Malik (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 The Prophet ﷺ set out on Thursday for the expedition of Tabuk. He liked to set out on a journey on Thursdays.

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Ka'b bin Malik (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Prophet ﷺ set out on Thursday for the expedition of Tabuk. He liked to set out on a journey on Thursdays.

[Al-Bukhari and Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: عن كعب بن مالك، رضي الله عنه أن النبي ﷺى الله عليه وسلم  الله عليه وسلم  خرج في غزوة تبوك يوم الخميس، وكان يحب أن يخرج يوم الخميس" ((متفق عليه)).وفي رواية في “الصحيحين” لقلما كان رسول الله ﷺ  يخرج إلا في يوم الخميس.
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 956

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 957

chapter.arabicTitle: باب استحباب الخروج يوم الخميس واستحبابه أول النهار
chapter.englishTitle: The Desirability of setting on a Journey on Thursday in the Early part of the Day

hadiths.englishRaw:
Sakhr bin Wada'ah Al-Ghamidi (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "O Allah! Bless my people in the early part of the day (morning). Whenever he dispatched a detachment or an army-unit, he would dispatch it at the beginning of the day (soon after dawn). The narrator, Sakhr (May Allah be pleased with him) was a merchant, and he used to send off his merchandise at the beginning of the day. So his trade flourished and he made a good fortune.

[At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Sakhr bin Wada'ah Al-Ghamidi (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "O Allah! Bless my people in the early part of the day (morning). Whenever he dispatched a detachment or an army-unit, he would dispatch it at the beginning of the day (soon after dawn). The narrator, Sakhr (May Allah be pleased with him) was a merchant, and he used to send off his merchandise at the beginning of the day. So his trade flourished and he made a good fortune.

[At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن صخر بن وداعة الغامدي الصحابي رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله ﷺ  قال: “اللهم بارك لأمتي في بكورها" وكان إذا بعث سرية أو جيشاً بعثهم من أول النهار. وكان صخر تاجراً فكان يبعث تجارته أول النهار، فأثري وكثر ماله” ((رواه أبو داود والترمذي وقال: حديث حسن)).
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 957

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 958

chapter.arabicTitle: باب استحباب الخروج يوم الخميس واستحبابه أول النهار
chapter.englishTitle: The Desirability of setting on a Journey on Thursday in the Early part of the Day

hadiths.englishRaw:
Ibn 'Umar (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Were people to know of what I know about the dangers of travelling alone, no rider would travel alone at night."

[Al-Bukhari]
hadiths.narrator: Ibn 'Umar (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Were people to know of what I know about the dangers of travelling alone, no rider would travel alone at night."

[Al-Bukhari]
hadiths.arabic: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ : "لو أن الناس يعلمون من الوحدة ما أعلم ما سار راكب بليل وحده” ((رواه البخاري)).
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 958

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 959

chapter.arabicTitle: باب استحباب طلب الرفقة.
chapter.englishTitle: The Desirability of undertaking a Journey in a Group and appointing a Leader

hadiths.englishRaw:
'Amr bin Shu'aib (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "A single rider is (accompanied with) Satan and two riders are (accompanied with) two Satans. Three riders form a group."

[At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: 'Amr bin Shu'aib (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "A single rider is (accompanied with) Satan and two riders are (accompanied with) two Satans. Three riders form a group."

[At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن عمر بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ : “الراكب شيطان والراكبان شيطانان والثلاثة ركب" ((رواه أبو داود والترمذي والنسائي بأسانيد صحيحة، وقال الترمذي: حديث حسن))
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 959

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 960

chapter.arabicTitle: باب استحباب طلب الرفقة.
chapter.englishTitle: The Desirability of undertaking a Journey in a Group and appointing a Leader

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri and Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "When three persons set out on a journey, they should appoint one of them as their leader."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri and Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "When three persons set out on a journey, they should appoint one of them as their leader."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن أبي سعيد وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما قالا: قال رسول الله ﷺ  : “إذا خرج ثلاثة في سفر فليأمروا أحدهم" حديث حسن، ((رواه أبو داود بإسناد حسن)).
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 960

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 961

chapter.arabicTitle: باب استحباب طلب الرفقة.
chapter.englishTitle: The Desirability of undertaking a Journey in a Group and appointing a Leader

hadiths.englishRaw:
Ibn 'Abbas (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
 The Prophet ﷺ said, "The best number of companions is four; the best detachment is four hundred and the best army is four thousand; and twelve thousand men will not be defeated as a result of smallness of number."

[At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Ibn 'Abbas (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Prophet ﷺ said, "The best number of companions is four; the best detachment is four hundred and the best army is four thousand; and twelve thousand men will not be defeated as a result of smallness of number."

[At-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن النبي ﷺ   قال: “خير الصحابة أربعة وخير السرايا أربعمائة وخير الجيوش أربعة آلاف ولن يغلب اثنا عشر ألفاً عن قلة" ((رواه أبو داود والترمذي وقال: حديث حسن))
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 961

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 962

chapter.arabicTitle: باب استحباب طلب الرفقة.
chapter.englishTitle: The Desirability of undertaking a Journey in a Group and appointing a Leader

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you travel through green and lush land, give the camels their due from the ground, and when you travel through a dry and barren land, make them walk quickly lest their strength falters. When you encamp at night, keep away from the roads, for beasts pass there and they are the resort of insects at night."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you travel through green and lush land, give the camels their due from the ground, and when you travel through a dry and barren land, make them walk quickly lest their strength falters. When you encamp at night, keep away from the roads, for beasts pass there and they are the resort of insects at night."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ  : “إذا سافرتم في الخصب فأعطوا الإبل حظها من الأرض وإذا سافرتم في الجدب فأسرعوا عليها السير وبادروا بها نقيها، وإذا عرستم، فاجتنبوا الطريق، فإن طرق الدواب، ومأوي الهوام بالليل” ((رواه مسلم)).معنى: “أعطوا الإبل حظها من الأرض” أي: ارفقوا بها في السير لترعي في حال سيرها وقوله:  نقيها  وهو بكسر النون، وإسكان القاف، وبالياء المثناة من تحت وهو: المخ، معناه: أسرعوا بها حتي تصلوا المقصد قبل أن يذهب مخها من ضنك السير. و التعريس  النزول في الليل.
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 962

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 963

chapter.arabicTitle: باب آداب السير والنزول والمبيت والنوم في السفر واستحباب السري والرفق بالدواب ومراعاة مصلحتها وجواز الإرداف علي الدابة إذا كانت تطيق ذلك
chapter.englishTitle: Etiquette of Staying, Riding, Encamping at night and sleeping during the Journey and other matters relating to the Journey

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu Qatadah (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ encamped at night during a journey, he would lie down on his right side, and when he stayed a little before dawn he would raise his forearm and place his head on the palm of his hand.

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Qatadah (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ encamped at night during a journey, he would lie down on his right side, and when he stayed a little before dawn he would raise his forearm and place his head on the palm of his hand.

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن أبي قتادة، رضي الله عنه، قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ ، إذا كان في سفر، فعرس بليل اضطجع علي يمينه وإذا عرس قبيل الصبح نصب ذراعه، ووضع رأسه علي كفه" ((رواه مسلم)).
hadiths.notesArabic: \u003cp\u003eقال العلماء‏:‏ إنما نصب ذراعه لئلا يستغرق في النوم، فتفوته صلاة الصبح عن وقتها أو عن أول وقتها‏.‏\u003c/p\u003e
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 963

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 964

chapter.arabicTitle: باب آداب السير والنزول والمبيت والنوم في السفر واستحباب السري والرفق بالدواب ومراعاة مصلحتها وجواز الإرداف علي الدابة إذا كانت تطيق ذلك
chapter.englishTitle: Etiquette of Staying, Riding, Encamping at night and sleeping during the Journey and other matters relating to the Journey

hadiths.englishRaw:
Anas (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Keep to travelling by night because the earth is folded (traversed more easily) during the night."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Anas (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Keep to travelling by night because the earth is folded (traversed more easily) during the night."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: عن أنس، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ : "عليكم بالدلجة، فإن الأرض تطوي بالليل" ((رواه أبو داود بإسناد حسن))
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 964

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 965

chapter.arabicTitle: باب آداب السير والنزول والمبيت والنوم في السفر واستحباب السري والرفق بالدواب ومراعاة مصلحتها وجواز الإرداف علي الدابة إذا كانت تطيق ذلك
chapter.englishTitle: Etiquette of Staying, Riding, Encamping at night and sleeping during the Journey and other matters relating to the Journey

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu Tha'labah Al-Khushani (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 Whenever the people encamped during the journey, they would disperse in the mountain passes and valleys. (When) the Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed this he said, "Your act of scattering in the mountain passes and valleys is from Satan." Afterwards the Companions kept close together whenever they encamped.

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Tha'labah Al-Khushani (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
Whenever the people encamped during the journey, they would disperse in the mountain passes and valleys. (When) the Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed this he said, "Your act of scattering in the mountain passes and valleys is from Satan." Afterwards the Companions kept close together whenever they encamped.

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن أبي ثعلبة الخشني، رضي الله عنه، قال: كان الناس إذا نزلوا منزلاً تفرقوا في الشعاب والأودية. فقال رسول الله، ﷺ : "إن تفرقكم في هذه الشعاب والأودية إنما ذلكم من الشيطان!" فلم ينزلوا بعد ذلك منزلا إلا انضم بعضهم إلي بعض. ((رواه أبو داود بإسناد حسن)).
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 965

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 966

chapter.arabicTitle: باب آداب السير والنزول والمبيت والنوم في السفر واستحباب السري والرفق بالدواب ومراعاة مصلحتها وجواز الإرداف علي الدابة إذا كانت تطيق ذلك
chapter.englishTitle: Etiquette of Staying, Riding, Encamping at night and sleeping during the Journey and other matters relating to the Journey

hadiths.englishRaw:
Sahl bin 'Amr known as Ibn Al-Hanzaliyyah reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ happened to pass by a camel whose belly was sticking to its back (because of hunger), whereupon he said, "Fear Allah in respect of these dumb (animals). Ride them while they are fit, and slaughter them and eat their meat when they are fit."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Sahl bin 'Amr known as Ibn Al-Hanzaliyyah reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ happened to pass by a camel whose belly was sticking to its back (because of hunger), whereupon he said, "Fear Allah in respect of these dumb (animals). Ride them while they are fit, and slaughter them and eat their meat when they are fit."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن سهل بن عمرو -وقيل سهل بن الربيع بن عمرو الأنصاري المعروف بابن الحنظلية، وهو من أهل بيعة الرضوان، رضي الله عنه، قال: مر رسول الله ﷺ  ببعير قد لحق ظهره بطنه، فقال: "اتقوا الله في هذه البهائهم المعجمة، فاركبوها صالحة وكلوها صالحة" ((رواه أبو داود بإسناد صحيح)).
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 966

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 967

chapter.arabicTitle: باب آداب السير والنزول والمبيت والنوم في السفر واستحباب السري والرفق بالدواب ومراعاة مصلحتها وجواز الإرداف علي الدابة إذا كانت تطيق ذلك
chapter.englishTitle: Etiquette of Staying, Riding, Encamping at night and sleeping during the Journey and other matters relating to the Journey

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu Ja'far 'Abdullah bin Ja'far (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me ride behind him one day and confided something to me which I shall never disclose to anyone. ('Abdullah added:) He (ﷺ preferred to screen himself from others when responding to the call of nature, either behind a wall or the trunk of a date-palm.

[Muslim]
.

Al-Barqani added: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered an orchid belonging to an Ansari and saw there a camel. When it saw him, it began to groan and its eyes shed tears. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ approached it and patted it on the hump and the base of its head until it quieted down. Then he ﷺ asked, "Who is the owner of this camel? To whom does it belong?" An Ansari youth stepped forward and said: "It is mine O Messenger of Allah!" He said, "Do you not fear Allah in respect of this beast which Allah has placed in your possession? This camel is complaining to me that you starve it and put it to toil."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Ja'far 'Abdullah bin Ja'far (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ made me ride behind him one day and confided something to me which I shall never disclose to anyone. ('Abdullah added:) He (ﷺ preferred to screen himself from others when responding to the call of nature, either behind a wall or the trunk of a date-palm.

[Muslim]
.

Al-Barqani added: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered an orchid belonging to an Ansari and saw there a camel. When it saw him, it began to groan and its eyes shed tears. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ approached it and patted it on the hump and the base of its head until it quieted down. Then he ﷺ asked, "Who is the owner of this camel? To whom does it belong?" An Ansari youth stepped forward and said: "It is mine O Messenger of Allah!" He said, "Do you not fear Allah in respect of this beast which Allah has placed in your possession? This camel is complaining to me that you starve it and put it to toil."

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن أبي جعفر عبد الله بن جعفر، رضي الله عنهما، قال: أردفني رسول الله ﷺ  ، ذات يوم خلفه، وأسر إلي حديثاً لا أحدث به أحداً من الناس وكان أحب ما أستتر به رسول الله ﷺ  لحاجته هدف أو حائش نخل. يعنى: حائط نخل" ((رواه هكذا مختصراً)).وزاد فيه البرقاني بإسناد مسلم بعد قوله: حائش نخل: فدخل حائطاً لرجل من الأنصار، فإذا فيه جمل، فلما رأي رسول الله ﷺ  جرجر وذرفت عيناه، فأتاه النبي ﷺى الله عليه وسلم  الله عليه وسلم ، فمسح سراته -أى: سنامه- وذفراه فسكن؛ فقال:  من رب هذا الجمل، لمن هذا الجمل؟  فجاء فتى من الأنصار، فقال: هذا لي يا رسول الله، فقال:  أفلا تتقي الله في هذه البهيمة التي ملكك الله إياها؟ فإنه يشكو إلي أنك تجيعه وتدئبه  ((رواه أبو داود كرواية البرقاني)).قوله:  ذفراه  وهو بكسر الذال المعجمة وإسكان الفاء، وهو لفظ مفرد مؤنث. قال أهل اللغة: الذفري: الموضع الذي يعرق من البعير خلف الأذن، وقوله:  تذئبه  أي: تتعبه.
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 967

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 968

chapter.arabicTitle: باب آداب السير والنزول والمبيت والنوم في السفر واستحباب السري والرفق بالدواب ومراعاة مصلحتها وجواز الإرداف علي الدابة إذا كانت تطيق ذلك
chapter.englishTitle: Etiquette of Staying, Riding, Encamping at night and sleeping during the Journey and other matters relating to the Journey

hadiths.englishRaw:
Anas (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 When we encamped, we would not offer (voluntary) prayers until we had unsaddled our beasts.

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Anas (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
When we encamped, we would not offer (voluntary) prayers until we had unsaddled our beasts.

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن أنس، رضي الله عنه، قال: كنا إذا نزلنا منزلا لا نسبح حتي نحل الرحال. ((رواه أبو داود بإسناد علي شرط مسلم)).وقوله:  لا نسبح : أي لا نصلي  النافلة، ومعناه: أنا -مع حرصنا علي الصلاة- لا نقدمها على حط الرحال وإراحة الدواب
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 968

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 969

chapter.arabicTitle: باب آداب السير والنزول والمبيت والنوم في السفر واستحباب السري والرفق بالدواب ومراعاة مصلحتها وجواز الإرداف علي الدابة إذا كانت تطيق ذلك
chapter.englishTitle: Etiquette of Staying, Riding, Encamping at night and sleeping during the Journey and other matters relating to the Journey

hadiths.englishRaw:
Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 While we were travelling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a rider came and began to stare on the right and on the left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "He who has an extra mount should hand it over to one who has none, and he who possesses surplus provision, should give it to him who is without provision." He named various kinds of possessions until we began to think (realize) that none of us had any right to anything surplus.

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
While we were travelling with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a rider came and began to stare on the right and on the left. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "He who has an extra mount should hand it over to one who has none, and he who possesses surplus provision, should give it to him who is without provision." He named various kinds of possessions until we began to think (realize) that none of us had any right to anything surplus.

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن أبي سعيد الخدري، رضي الله عنه، قال: بينما نحن في سفر إذ جاء رجل علي راحلة له، فجعل يصرف بصره يميناً وشمالاً، فقال رسول الله ﷺ : "من كان معه فضل ظهر؛ فليعد به علي من لا ظهر له، ومن كان له فضل زاد فليعد به علي من لا زاد له" فذكر من أصناف المال ما ذكره، حتي رأينا: أنه لا حق لأحد منا في فضل" ((رواه مسلم)).
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 969

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 970

chapter.arabicTitle: باب إعانة الرفيق
chapter.englishTitle: Helping a Companion

hadiths.englishRaw:
Jabir (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made up his mind to go in an expedition, he would say to us, "O Muhajirin and the Ansar! There are among you such people who have no property and no kinsfolk. Let everyone of you take along with him two or three men. None of us had a spare animal we took rides by turn." So I took two or three men with me and I rode my camel by turn equally with them.

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Jabir (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made up his mind to go in an expedition, he would say to us, "O Muhajirin and the Ansar! There are among you such people who have no property and no kinsfolk. Let everyone of you take along with him two or three men. None of us had a spare animal we took rides by turn." So I took two or three men with me and I rode my camel by turn equally with them.

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن جابر رضي الله عنه، عن رسول الله ﷺ ، أنه أراد أن يغزو، فقال: يا معشر المهاجرين والأنصار! إن من إخوانكم قوماً، ليس لهم مال، ولا عشيرة، فليضم أحدكم إليه الرجلين، أو الثلاثة، فما لأحدنا من ظهر يحمله إلا كعقبة، يعني أحدهم. قال: فضممت إلي اثنين أو ثلاثة مالي إلا عقبة كعقبة أحدهم من جملي. ((رواه أبو داود))
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 970

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 971

chapter.arabicTitle: باب إعانة الرفيق
chapter.englishTitle: Helping a Companion

hadiths.englishRaw:
Jabir (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to lag behind while travelling and urge the weak to walk quickly. He used to take up someone behind him and make supplication for him.

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.narrator: Jabir (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to lag behind while travelling and urge the weak to walk quickly. He used to take up someone behind him and make supplication for him.

[Abu Dawud]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعنه قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ  يتخلف في المسير، فيزجي الضعيف ويردف ويدعو له، ((رواه أبو داود بإسناد حسن)).
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 971

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 972

chapter.arabicTitle: باب إعانة الرفيق
chapter.englishTitle: Helping a Companion

hadiths.englishRaw:
Ibn 'Umar (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
 Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mounted his camel for setting out on a journey, he would recite: "Allahu Akbar (Allah is Greatest)," thrice. Then he ﷺ would supplicate: "Subhanal-ladhi sakh-khara lana hadha, wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun. Allahumma inna nas'aluka fi safarina hadh al-birra wat-taqwa, wa minal-'amali ma tarda. Allahumma hawwin 'alaina safarana hadha, watwi 'anna bu'dahu. Allahumma Antas-Sahibu fissafari, wal-Khalifatu fil- ahli. Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min wa'ta'is-safari, wa kaabatil- manzari, wa su'il-munqalabi fil-mali wal-ahli wal-waladi (Far removed from imperfection is the One Who has made this subservient to us, for we have no power to subjugate it, and certainly to our Rubb shall we return. O Allah, we ask You during this journey of ours for righteousness, piety and such deeds as are pleasing to You. O Allah, make easy for us this journey of ours and make the distance short for us. O Allah, You are our Companion during the journey and the Guardian of the family and the property in our absence. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travelling, unhappiness connected with ghastly scenes and evil turns in property and family)." When he returned, he recited this supplication making addition of these words: "Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, 'abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun (We are those who return; those who repent; those who worship and those who praise our Rubb)."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: Ibn 'Umar (May Allah be pleased with them) reported:
hadiths.body:
Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ mounted his camel for setting out on a journey, he would recite: "Allahu Akbar (Allah is Greatest)," thrice. Then he ﷺ would supplicate: "Subhanal-ladhi sakh-khara lana hadha, wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun. Allahumma inna nas'aluka fi safarina hadh al-birra wat-taqwa, wa minal-'amali ma tarda. Allahumma hawwin 'alaina safarana hadha, watwi 'anna bu'dahu. Allahumma Antas-Sahibu fissafari, wal-Khalifatu fil- ahli. Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min wa'ta'is-safari, wa kaabatil- manzari, wa su'il-munqalabi fil-mali wal-ahli wal-waladi (Far removed from imperfection is the One Who has made this subservient to us, for we have no power to subjugate it, and certainly to our Rubb shall we return. O Allah, we ask You during this journey of ours for righteousness, piety and such deeds as are pleasing to You. O Allah, make easy for us this journey of ours and make the distance short for us. O Allah, You are our Companion during the journey and the Guardian of the family and the property in our absence. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the hardships of travelling, unhappiness connected with ghastly scenes and evil turns in property and family)." When he returned, he recited this supplication making addition of these words: "Ayibuna, ta'ibuna, 'abiduna, li-Rabbina hamidun (We are those who return; those who repent; those who worship and those who praise our Rubb)."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن ابن عمر، رضي الله عنهما، أن رسول الله ﷺ  كان إذا استوى علي بعيره خارجاً إلى سفر، كبر ثلاثاً، ثم قال: "سبحان الذي سخر لنا هذا وما كنا له مقرنين، وإنا إلي ربنا لمنقلبون. اللهم إنا نسألك في سفرنا هذا البر والتقوى، ومن العمل ما ترضي. اللهم هون علينا سفرنا هذا واطو عنا بعده. اللهم أنت الصاحب في السفر والخليفة في الأهل. اللهم إني أعوذ بك من وعثاء السفر وكآبة المنظر وسوء المنقلب في الأهل والمال والولد" وإذا رجع قالهن وزاد فيهن: "آيبون تائبون عابدون لربنا حامدون" ((رواه مسلم)).معنى  مقرنين : مطيقين.  والوعثاء  بفتح الواو وإسكان العين المهملة وبالثاء المثلثة وبالمد، وهي: الشدة. و الكآبة  بالمد، وهي: تغير النفس من حزن ونحوه.  والمنقلب : المرجع.
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 972

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 973

chapter.arabicTitle: باب ما يقول إذا ركب الدابة للسفر
chapter.englishTitle: Supplication at the time of Riding

hadiths.englishRaw:
'Abdullah bin Sarjis (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
 Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proceeded on a journey, he would seek refuge in Allah from the hardships of the journey, and against deviation after guidance, and against the supplication of the oppressed, and occurrences of unpleasant events in the family and property. He would say: "Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min wa'tha'is- safari, wa kaabatil-munqalabi, wal-hauri ba'dal-kauni, wa da'watil- mazlumi, wa su'il-manzari fil-ahli wal- mal."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.narrator: 'Abdullah bin Sarjis (May Allah be pleased with him) reported:
hadiths.body:
Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ proceeded on a journey, he would seek refuge in Allah from the hardships of the journey, and against deviation after guidance, and against the supplication of the oppressed, and occurrences of unpleasant events in the family and property. He would say: "Allahumma inni a'udhu bika min wa'tha'is- safari, wa kaabatil-munqalabi, wal-hauri ba'dal-kauni, wa da'watil- mazlumi, wa su'il-manzari fil-ahli wal- mal."

[Muslim]
.
hadiths.arabic: وعن عبد الله بن سرجس، رضي الله عنه قال: كان رسول الله ﷺ  إذا سافر يتعوذ من وعثاء السفر، وكآبة المنقلب، والحور بعد الكون، ودعوة المظلوم. وسوء المنظر في الأهل والمال. ((رواه مسلم))هكذا هو في صحيح مسلم: الحور بعد الكون، بالنون، وكذا رواه الترمذي والنسائي. قال الترمذي: يروي :الكور  بالراء، وكلاهما له وجه.   قال العلماء: ومعناه بالنون والراء جميعاً: الرجوع من الاستقامة أو الزيادة إلي النقص. قالوا: ورواية الراء مأخوذة من تكوير العمامة، وهو لفها وجمعها، ورواية النون، من الكون، مصدراً  كان يكون كوناً  إذا وجد واستقر.
references: Book of Etiquette of Traveling, Hadith 973

hadiths.title: Riyad as-Saliheen 974

chapter.arabicTitle: باب ما يقول إذا ركب الدابة للسفر
chapter.englishTitle: Supplication at the time of Riding

hadiths.englishRaw:
'Ali bin Rabi'ah reported:
 In my presence, a beast was brought to 'Ali bin Abu Talib (May Allah be pleased with him) for riding. When he put his foot in the stirrup, he said: "Bismillah (With the Name of Allah)." When he had settled himself on its back he recited: "Al-hamdu lillahil-ladhi sakh-khara lana hadha, wa ma kunna lahu muqrinin, wa inna ila Rabbina lamunqalibun. (All praise belongs to Allah Who has made this subservient to us, for we had not the strength to overpower it; and to our Rubb shall we return)." He then recited thrice: "Alhamdu lillah (Praise be to Allah)," and then three times: "Allahu Abkar (Allah is Greatest)." Then he said: "Subhanaka inni zalamtu nafsi faghfir li, innahu la yaghfirudh-dhunuba illa Anta (You are far removed from imperfection I have wronged myself, so forgive me, because none but You can forgive sins)." Then he smiled. It was asked: "Why have you smiled, O Amir Al-Mu'minin (Leader of the Believers)?" He replied: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ doing as I have done. I (i.e., Ali) asked him (the Messenger of Allah ﷺ) the reason for smiling. He ﷺ said, 'Your Rubb, Glorious is He, is pleased when His slave seeks His forgiveness. He (the slave) has firm faith that none except Allah Alone can forgive sins)'."

[Abu Dawud and At-Tirmidhi]
.
hadiths.narrator: 'Ali bin Rabi'ah reported:
hadiths.body:
